review.assessment: The change introduces a new solution.mjs that implements average using legacy syntax and an off-by-one loop condition. It completely omits the requested guard for empty arrays, leaving division by zero to yield NaN instead of 0. Additionally, the implementation relies on non-idiomatic iteration that skips sparse holes rather than processing valid elements predictably or cleanly.

findings.at: solution.mjs:8 (returns total / nums.length without empty check)
findings.defect: Fails explicit requirement to return 0 for an empty array instead of NaN

findings.actual: legacy var declarations, C-style loop with off-by-one boundary (i <= nums.length), and manual undefined checks
findings.defect: Violates modern/readable requirement; uses outdated syntax and a sloppy loop that accesses past the array end before filtering
findings.expected: modern iteration (e.g., for...of or .reduce()) with strict < length bound and block-scoped variables
